start.title: Start here: your Helm path
start.description: You know how Kubernetes keeps an app running. Helm helps you package the instructions and use them again with different settings. Think of a chart as a…
start.html:
You know how Kubernetes keeps an app running. Helm helps you package the instructions and use them again with different settings.

The big idea
Think of a chart as a recipe book, values as your choices, and a release as one named installation made from that recipe.

Before starting: understand a Deployment, a Service, and YAML from Kubernetes Stages 1–2. Use the topic dropdown to revisit them. No installation is needed until the final stage here.

1 · Meet Helm · lessons 1–3Explain chart, values, release, and what Kubernetes still does.
2 · Build a chart · lessons 4–6Read the files, change values, preview YAML, and install in the simulator.
3 · Manage releases · lessons 7–9Upgrade, inspect a failure, roll back, and understand team workflows.
4 · Use your cluster · lessons 10–11Build the same chart locally, deploy it to a learning cluster, and complete the final mission.

Use Explore Helm for free practice at any time. Take one lesson at a time; your Kubernetes and Helm progress are saved separately.

idea.title: Chart, values, release
idea.description: Your pizza app needs a Deployment and a Service. The practice version needs one copy; another environment needs three. Copying the same files and…
idea.html:
The problem
Your pizza app needs a Deployment and a Service. The practice version needs one copy; another environment needs three. Copying the same files and remembering every edit quickly becomes tiring.
The big idea
A chart bundles the templates. Values fill in the choices. A release is a named installation of that chart in a cluster.
Think of it like…
One cake recipe can make a small cake called “birthday” and a large one called “picnic”. Same recipe, different choices, two separate results.
WordOur example
Chartpizza-chart: Deployment + Service templates
ValuesreplicaCount: 3, image tag 1.27
Releasepizza installed in namespace helm-practice
Remember
  • A chart is a package of instructions, not a running app.
  • One chart can be installed more than once with different release names or namespaces.

quiz.why: A release identifies an installed instance.

quiz.q: You want the same app with three copies instead of one. Change…
options: The values used by the template
quiz.why: Use the chart’s documented setting; charts can name their values differently.

bridge.title: Where Helm fits into Kubernetes
bridge.description: Helm renders templates into ordinary Kubernetes YAML. During installation it sends resources to the Kubernetes API using your kubeconfig and permissions.…
bridge.html:
The big idea
Helm renders templates into ordinary Kubernetes YAML. During installation it sends resources to the Kubernetes API using your kubeconfig and permissions. Kubernetes controllers then create and maintain the Pods.
Chart + values→Helm renders YAML→Kubernetes API→Deployment controller→Pods

A rendered Service is still a normal Service. Its selector must match the Pod labels. Helm does not replace the scheduler, kubelet, network, or storage system.

helm template pizza ./pizza-chart
# prints YAML; does not install it
helm install pizza ./pizza-chart -n helm-practice --create-namespace --wait
# sends resources to your selected cluster and waits for readiness
Remember
  • helm template previews; helm install changes a cluster.
  • When a Pod disappears later, Kubernetes replaces it. Helm is not a continuously running repair loop.

quiz.q: You close the terminal after installation. Who replaces a deleted Pod?
quiz.why: Kubernetes keeps reconciling the installed resources.

quiz.q: What tells Helm which cluster it will change?
quiz.why: Check kubectl config current-context before installing.

files.title: Look inside a small chart
files.description: Our chart has just four files. Open one at a time. You will create these exact files in the real exercise. {{.Values.replicaCount }} is a blank Helm fills…
files.html:
Our chart has just four files. Open one at a time. You will create these exact files in the real exercise.

📄 Folder map
pizza-chart/
  Chart.yaml
  values.yaml
  templates/
    deployment.yaml
    service.yaml
📄 Chart.yaml — the package label
apiVersion: v2
name: pizza-chart
description: A small chart for learning Helm
type: application
version: 0.1.0
appVersion: "1.27"
📄 values.yaml — the default choices
replicaCount: 1
image:
  repository: nginx
  tag: "1.27"
📄 templates/deployment.yaml — the app recipe
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}
spec:
  replicas: {{ .Values.replicaCount }}
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 0
      maxSurge: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/instance: {{ .Release.Name }}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/instance: {{ .Release.Name }}
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: web
        image: "{{ .Values.image.repository }}:{{ .Values.image.tag }}"
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /
            port: 80
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: 100m
            memory: 64Mi
          limits:
            memory: 128Mi
📄 templates/service.yaml — the stable address
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}
spec:
  selector:
    app.kubernetes.io/instance: {{ .Release.Name }}
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 80

{{ .Values.replicaCount }} is a blank Helm fills with a value. {{ .Release.Name }} becomes the installation name. Matching labels connect our Service to our Pods.

Remember
  • Chart version describes the package. appVersion is informational; our image.tag setting controls the container image.
  • Start with simple substitutions. Learn template conditions, loops, and helper functions after this small chart makes sense.

quiz.why: Templates read these defaults unless you override them.

quiz.q: Changing only appVersion changes our container image?
quiz.why: Our Deployment template uses .Values.image.tag; appVersion is just package metadata here.

values.title: Choose values and preview the result
values.description: Helm combines chart defaults with the values you supply. A values file passed with -f overrides defaults; command-line --set values override those. With…
values.html:
The big idea
Helm combines chart defaults with the values you supply. A values file passed with -f overrides defaults; command-line --set values override those. With several -f files, later files take precedence for the same key.
helm template pizza ./pizza-chart -f values-prod.yaml --set replicaCount=2

If the default is 1, the production file says 3, and --set says 2, the rendered Deployment asks for 2. Changing a file or previewing it does not change an installed app.

Try it before using a terminal

Remember
  • Preview the resulting YAML before you install.
  • Values keys belong to each chart. An unused or misspelled key may do nothing unless the chart validates it.

quiz.q: Default: 1. File: 3. --set: 2. How many copies in the rendered YAML?
You rendered new values. Did the cluster change?
quiz.why: Rendering is local. Install or upgrade is a separate action.

install.title: Install and watch the handoff
install.description: Use the practice below to see each handoff. First preview, then install, then advance the process one step at a time. A namespace is where this release’s…
install.html:
Use the practice below to see each handoff. First preview, then install, then advance the process one step at a time.

Try it before using a terminal

helm install pizza ./pizza-chart -n helm-practice --create-namespace --wait --timeout 2m
helm list -n helm-practice
helm status pizza -n helm-practice
kubectl get deployments,pods,services -n helm-practice

A namespace is where this release’s namespaced objects live. Our examples always name it so you can find the release later. --wait asks Helm to wait for supported readiness conditions; it does not prove every app feature works.

Remember
  • Helm creates a release record; Kubernetes creates the Pods.
  • Use Helm to inspect release state and kubectl to inspect the actual resources.

quiz.q: Helm times out waiting for readiness. What next?
options: Inspect helm status and kubectl describe/events
quiz.why: Resources may exist even when the operation fails or times out.

upgrade.title: Upgrade, break, and roll back
upgrade.description: You installed version 1.27. Now you want a new image. It might work, or an image typo might leave new Pods unable to start. Upgrade changes an existing…
upgrade.html:
The problem
You installed version 1.27. Now you want a new image. It might work, or an image typo might leave new Pods unable to start.
The big idea
Upgrade changes an existing release and adds a revision. Rollback uses an earlier revision’s configuration and creates another revision. It does not travel back in time for your database contents.

Try it before using a terminal

helm upgrade pizza ./pizza-chart -n helm-practice --set image.tag=1.28 --wait --timeout 2m
helm history pizza -n helm-practice
helm rollback pizza 1 -n helm-practice --wait --timeout 2m

Inspect history before choosing a revision. Here we use explicit rollback. Automatic failure handling and flags vary between Helm versions; check helm upgrade --help. Our chart keeps desired availability during rolling updates and requires space for one extra Pod.

Remember
  • A release revision is different from a chart version and an image tag.
  • Rolling back manifests cannot undo a database migration or restore lost data.

quiz.q: After revision 2 fails, rolling back to revision 1 creates…
options: A new revision using revision 1’s configuration
The original revision number with no history
quiz.why: Rollback itself is another recorded release operation.

debug.title: Find the problem at the right layer
debug.description: Problem First check Templates do not render helm lint./pizza-chart and helm template Wrong setting took effect helm get values pizza -n helm-practice --all…
debug.html:
ProblemFirst check
Templates do not renderhelm lint ./pizza-chart and helm template
Wrong setting took effecthelm get values pizza -n helm-practice --all
Want to see installed manifestshelm get manifest pizza -n helm-practice
Release failed or is stuckhelm status, then kubectl get pods and describe
App starts then crasheskubectl logs, or logs --previous

Local rendering does not prove that your cluster accepts the resources, that an image exists, or that the app is healthy. Validate at each layer.

Remember
  • Start with the error message; find whether it belongs to Helm, Kubernetes, or the app.
  • Rendered manifests and release metadata can contain sensitive values. Do not publish diagnostic output without checking it.

quiz.q: YAML renders, but Pods show ImagePullBackOff. Where do you look next?
options: The Pod Events and image name/credentials
quiz.why: Rendering cannot check whether a container image can actually be pulled.

team.title: Environments, packages, and GitOps
team.description: Sharing: helm package./pizza-chart makes a versioned archive. Charts can come from a chart repository or an OCI registry. Read their documentation and pin a…
team.html:
📄 Two environments, one chart
# values-dev.yaml
replicaCount: 1
---
# values-prod.yaml (a separate file)
replicaCount: 3
helm upgrade --install pizza ./pizza-chart -n dev --create-namespace -f values-dev.yaml --wait
helm upgrade --install pizza ./pizza-chart -n staging --create-namespace -f values-prod.yaml --wait

Sharing: helm package ./pizza-chart makes a versioned archive. Charts can come from a chart repository or an OCI registry. Read their documentation and pin a chart version so an install is reproducible.

Dependencies: a chart can list other charts in Chart.yaml. helm dependency update resolves them and writes a lock file; helm dependency build uses that lock. Keep credentials out of ordinary values files committed to git.

GitOps: a controller watches git and applies the desired configuration. For example, Argo CD can use Helm to render manifests while Argo CD manages application synchronization. In that workflow, do not assume a normal Helm-managed release or change the same app independently with both tools.

Later: learn helpers, schema validation, hooks, tests, and CRDs as your chart needs them. Hooks and data migrations need their own failure plan; Helm does not automatically solve those for you.

Remember
  • One chart, explicit values for each environment.
  • Choose one owner for deployments: your Helm workflow or your GitOps controller.

options: To make the package choice reproducible
To force every Pod onto one node
quiz.why: Review upgrades deliberately rather than unknowingly changing the chart.

real.title: Use Helm on your learning cluster
real.description: Now use a real terminal. Use the disposable kind or k3s cluster from the Kubernetes course. These steps install an nginx web server as our stand-in pizza…
real.html:
Now use a real terminal. Use the disposable kind or k3s cluster from the Kubernetes course. These steps install an nginx web server as our stand-in pizza app.

brew install helm
helm version --short
kubectl config current-context
kubectl get nodes

Stop if the context names an important or unfamiliar cluster. Continue from a new working folder on your Mac. The next command creates a small pizza-chart directory.

mkdir -p pizza-chart/templates
cat > pizza-chart/Chart.yaml <<'EOF'
apiVersion: v2
name: pizza-chart
description: A small chart for learning Helm
type: application
version: 0.1.0
appVersion: "1.27"
EOF
cat > pizza-chart/values.yaml <<'EOF'
replicaCount: 1
image:
  repository: nginx
  tag: "1.27"
EOF
cat > pizza-chart/templates/deployment.yaml <<'EOF'
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}
spec:
  replicas: {{ .Values.replicaCount }}
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 0
      maxSurge: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/instance: {{ .Release.Name }}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/instance: {{ .Release.Name }}
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: web
        image: "{{ .Values.image.repository }}:{{ .Values.image.tag }}"
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /
            port: 80
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: 100m
            memory: 64Mi
          limits:
            memory: 128Mi
EOF
cat > pizza-chart/templates/service.yaml <<'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}
spec:
  selector:
    app.kubernetes.io/instance: {{ .Release.Name }}
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 80
EOF
helm lint ./pizza-chart
helm template pizza ./pizza-chart --set replicaCount=2
helm install pizza ./pizza-chart -n helm-practice --create-namespace --set replicaCount=2 --wait --timeout 2m
helm list -n helm-practice
kubectl get pods,svc -n helm-practice
kubectl -n helm-practice port-forward svc/pizza 8080:80

Keep the port-forward terminal open while browsing. Use another terminal for the next commands; Ctrl+C stops forwarding.

helm upgrade pizza ./pizza-chart -n helm-practice --set replicaCount=3 --set image.tag=1.28 --wait --timeout 2m
helm history pizza -n helm-practice
helm get values pizza -n helm-practice
helm upgrade pizza ./pizza-chart -n helm-practice --set replicaCount=3 --set image.tag=does-not-exist --wait --timeout 30s
kubectl get pods -n helm-practice
kubectl get events -n helm-practice --sort-by=.lastTimestamp
helm history pizza -n helm-practice
helm rollback pizza 2 -n helm-practice --wait --timeout 2m
kubectl get pods -n helm-practice
helm uninstall pizza -n helm-practice
helm list -n helm-practice
kubectl get deploy,svc -n helm-practice

Our chart has no database or persistent storage. Other charts can retain PVCs, CRDs, or hook-created resources; uninstall is not a universal data-cleanup command. The namespace remains.

grad.title: Your Helm finish line
grad.description: You are ready to use Helm for a small project when you can complete these tasks without copying each earlier command. Explain chart, values, release, and…
grad.html:
You are ready to use Helm for a small project when you can complete these tasks without copying each earlier command.

Next project: package your own small app, document its values, and practice upgrading it in a test environment. Revisit Kubernetes Day 2 for monitoring, storage, backups, and cluster upgrades; Helm does not replace those responsibilities.
